phrases.text: So welcome back again.
Time for one more problem.
Now, in this problem, we are given that one cyclist is twenty-four kilometer behind another cyclist.
The speed of the faster cyclist is fifty-four kilometer per hour.
The speed of the slower cyclist is forty-two kilometer
per hour.
The question is asking us to find
how long the faster cyclist will take to overtake the slower cyclist.
Now, let us understand what is actually happening.
In one hour,
the slower cyclist moves forty-two kilometer.
At the same time,
the faster cyclist moves fifty-four kilometer.
The faster cyclist covers the extra distance,
which is fifty-four minus forty-two.
That is twelve kilometer.
So in one hour, the gap reduces by only twelve kilometer.
Got it?
Perfect.
Now, the total gap between them is twenty-four kilometer.
If twelve kilometer of the gap is reduced in one hour,
then one kilometer of the gap will be reduced in one divided by twelve hour.
Therefore,
to reduce a gap of twenty-four kilometer,
the time taken will be twenty-four into one by twelve. That is equal to twenty-four
divided by twelve.
This gives us two hours.
Now, let me tell you the formula for these types of questions.
Whenever two objects are moving in the same direction, always use the difference of their speeds. This is called the relative speed.
So relative speed equals fifty-four minus forty-two
equals twelve kilometer per hour. The distance to be covered is twenty-four
kilometer. Now, simply use the

formula, time equals distance divided by relative speed. Time equals twenty-four divided by twelve equals two hours. So the faster cyclist will overtake the slower cyclist after two hours. Hence, the correct answer is option
B.
